row.Finding description: Ratiometric OregonGreen measurements across three independent biological and technical replicate experiments showed higher lysosomal pH in human APOE4-expressing murine Neuro-2a cells (pH 5.86) than in APOE3-expressing cells (pH 4.30) or parental cells without human APOE (pH 4.58).
row.Finding quote: We found that HsAPOE4-expressing cells exhibit dramatic lysosomal alkalinization (pH = 5.86) compared to HsAPOE3 (pH = 4.30) cells (Figure 1C–E), reminiscent of previous results in APOE4-expressing astrocyte lysosomes (pH = 5.20, compared to pH = 4.08 in APOE3 astrocytes) [26]. This alkalinization was also observed in comparison to the parental cell line in which no human APOE had been introduced (referred to as HsAPOE−/−, pH = 4.58).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (higher lysosomal pH in murine Neuro-2a cells)
row.Experimental system: Male murine Neuro-2a neuroblastoma cell lines expressing transgenic full-length human APOE3 or APOE4, compared with parental cells lacking human APOE; endogenous murine Apoe remained intact; passages 5–10. Lysosomal pH was measured by calibrated ratiometric confocal imaging after overnight loading with OregonGreen 488–dextran (70,000 MW) beginning on culture day 3 and a 1-hour chase the following day.
